title: Normalize an audio segment, and quiet system audio shows and sounds right
goal: User 2026-09-26: 'when we have audio tracks, I'd like an option to normalize the audio. Recording with system audio seems to barely register on the audio histogram on the tracks.' Two parts: a Normalize action like Premiere's Audio Gain > Normalize (and Final Cut's loudness), and finding out why system audio records so quiet: whether the capture itself is low (ScreenCaptureKit system-audio level, mixing with the mic) or the waveform draws on a linear scale so quiet audio looks flat. Reproduce with a real recording that has system audio before changing anything.
acceptance: Reproduced first: record 10 s of system audio at a normal listening volume, measure its peak and loudness (dBFS / LUFS) from the file, and photograph its waveform; say whether the capture is quiet, the drawing is misleading, or both

Right-click an audio segment (or several selected): Normalize, bringing peaks to -1 dBFS by default; Normalize to Loudness in the same submenu targets -14 LUFS (web) or -16 LUFS (podcast); the gain is a non-destructive value on the segment, undoable, and shown on the segment as a small +N dB label
A Gain row in the panel for a selected audio segment shows the current gain in dB and can be dragged or typed, and a Normalize button sits beside it
The waveform draws on a scale that makes quiet speech and system audio visible (dB-scaled or auto-scaled per track, as Premiere does), and redraws when gain changes
If the capture is quiet: system audio is recorded at unity level, and new recordings with system audio can be normalized automatically on open (one checkbox in Settings, on by default)
The mix meter and export honour the gain; normalizing never clips (the existing loudness guard still applies)
A walk at Next defaults opens a recording with quiet system audio, normalizes it from the right-click menu, and photographs the waveform before and after

log.note: Reproduced. (1) The user's recent recordings are quiet in the FILE: ffmpeg ebur128/volumedetect on ~/Pictures/Screenshots 'Recording 2026-09-25 at 08.01.27.mp4' peak -27.3 dBFS / -40.0 LUFS; '04.52.10' -24.9 dBFS / -39.5 LUFS; '2026-09-06 22.29.13' -36.7 dBFS / -65.1 LUFS; '2026-09-02' -45.3 dBFS / -63.3 LUFS. (2) The capture itself is at unity: new probe-only --audio-capture-diag records through the real ScreenRecorder (SCRecordingOutput, system audio) while afplay plays a -9.0 dBFS tone; the recording read back -8.7 dBFS peak with the Mac's output volume at 6 of 100. So SCK takes system audio before the output volume and adds no attenuation; with --with-microphone the pre-tone stretch read -91 dB (the probe has no mic grant), so mic mixing is unverified. (3) The drawing IS misleading: SoundFile.peaks is linear and SoundWaveform draws column*halfHeight, so a -30 dBFS peak is 3% of the lane. Verdict: capture not quiet, sources quiet, drawing misleading. Plan: dB-scaled waveform that follows gain, a non-destructive clip gain (dB) on the level, Normalize (peaks -1 dBFS) and Normalize Loudness (-14/-16 LUFS, BS.1770) from the right-click menu and a Gain row in the Sound panel. The auto-normalize-on-open checkbox is conditional on a quiet capture, which it is not; left to the user as an audit question. Checked: AVMutableAudioMix setVolumeRamp and AVAudioMixerNode.volume both honour x50 linearly (quiet.m4a peak 0.011 -> 0.551), so gain rides the existing ramps.

Built: AudioLevel.clipGainDB (-48..+48, multiplies every ramp so playback, export, meter and headroom guard honour it); AudioNormalize (peak from waveform over played pieces; loudness targets -14/-16 capped at -1 dBFS peak); LoudnessMeter (BS.1770, calibration test -3.01 LUFS passes); SoundFile.loudnessLUFS; Waveform.drawnHeight (dB scale, 54 dB range, follows gain). App: right-click Normalize > Peaks to -1 dB / Loudness for Web / Podcast, Reset Gain (acts on every picked sound, one undo); Sound panel Gain row (slider + typed box) with Normalize under it; +N dB tag on the segment. Walk normalize-quiet-system-audio-walk at Next defaults: ok, 4 real captures; Loudness for Web gave +28.7 dB, matching ffmpeg's -42.7 LUFS reading. Neighbouring walks (linked sound, sound on the timeline, fades, mix meter, scrub, keyframes, panel order) ok. Full suite 9,985 green. Not built: auto-normalize-on-open (conditional on a quiet capture, which it is not; asked in the audit). Left rough, not filed: Normalize Loudness on a long file lands after a pause with no progress shown (audit rough).

Reproduced first: capture is at unity (-9.0 dBFS tone recorded at -8.7 with volume 6/100), the user's recordings are quiet at the source (-25 to -45 dBFS peaks), and the linear waveform hid them.
